newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Sacked S.Korean defence chief indicted for bribery.
newsitem.headline: Sacked S.Korean defence chief indicted for bribery.

text.p: Former South Korean defence minister Lee Yang-ho, sacked last month, was formally indicted on Monday on charges of bribery and leaking state secrets, a prosecution official said.

Also indicted in a case that has rocked the military establishment and embarassed President Kim Young-sam were the former head of Daewoo Heavy Industries, a unit of the mighty Daewoo Group, and two others.
But charges were dropped against the only daughter of one-time President Roh Tae-woo, accused of accepting diamond jewellery offered to gain a promotion for Lee.
Lee was charged with taking 150 million won ($181,000) as part of his share of payments to an arms dealer in connection with a military purchase of helicopters from Daewoo.
Prosecutors charge he leaked classified information on helicopter purchase plans to the Korean-American arms dealer, Kwon Pyong-ho.
The former head of Daewoo Heavy Industries, Sok Chin-chol, who now heads Daewoo's car subsidiary in Poland, was also indicted on bribery charges.
Two employees of the arms dealer were indicted for extorting 50 million won from Lee by threatening to expose the kickbacks, the prosecution official said.
The prosecution alleges Lee and the arms dealer split a 300 million won payment from Daewoo Heavy. The company says it paid the money as a commission.
The prosecution official said charges against Roh's daughter, So-young, were dropped because she promptly returned the gems presented by the wife of the arms dealer.
Roh Tae-woo is now appealing against a 22-1/2 year jail sentence imposed for bribery, treason and mutiny. His predecessor, Chun Doo Hwan, is trying to escape a death sentence on similar charges.
Lee was sacked as Defence Minister hours before allegations of the pay-offs surfaced in parliament.
He was arrested on October 26 and taken to a detention centre. Prosecutors then said he had admitted to receiving the money, although Lee has never commented in public on the charges.

President Kim has staked his reputation on rooting out corruption from Korean society, and the latest scandal was a double embarassment to him coming on the heels of a security scare involving a North Korean submarine.
The vessel brazenly sailed past South Korean warships to land 26 North Koreans on a beach in September.
Lee's dismissal was part of a wider shake up of the military top brass to take responsiblity for the submarine fiasco.
Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-choong is appealing a two year jail sentence for bribing ex-president Roh.
